naslov: Do Not Exalt Yourself by Humiliating a Sinner

segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

…the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Dear brothers, respected members of the congregation, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, created man and made him prone to sin.

And He made him prone to sin, which both the hadiths and the verses confirm for us. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says that every person, every son of Adam, sins, but the best of them is the one who repents.
And every person, my dear brothers, has the right to repentance, has the right to repentance, to a second chance, until death comes to him or until the sun rises from the west.
Unfortunately, here in these lands of ours we have a rather strange attitude towards those, towards those brothers who repent for their sins and return to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

So, rarely or more often, you will hear the words of some ignorant people who say: "You did this and that, do you remember when you did this and that?", reproaching their brother for what he once did, for the sins he once committed.

What does Ibn al-Qayyim, rahimahullahu ta'ala, say? He says: your reproaching a Muslim brother for a sin he committed is sometimes a greater sin and a greater disobedience than the very sin he committed.
Than the very sin he committed. Unfortunately, a lot of this happens in our society. A lot. There are many people who return to the religion of Allah.

There are many people who return to the religion of Allah. And there are also many who would like to return, to come to the mosque, to perform the prayer, but they are afraid precisely of that reproach: what will other people say?
And believe me, dear brothers, sometimes the one who starts coming and performing the prayer does so sincerely for the sake of Allah and leaves all those sins behind.

And believe me, sometimes such a person becomes better than the one who has been praying for years. Sometimes it happens that he understands the religion better than the one who has been praying for decades.

An example of this for us is Umar, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu. When did Umar accept Islam? In the sixth year of the prophethood. Imagine, in the sixth year after the prophethood. And yet he was better than the other companions. Far better.

We have the example of Abu Hurayrah, who accepted Islam in the seventh year after the Hijra, and he narrated over five thousand hadiths. And there are companions who accepted Islam at the very beginning, but Abu Hurayrah surpassed them. And that is why, dear brothers, a person must not become arrogant because of his obedience, must not become arrogant.

So that he says: "I pray this much and that much", and then, if he sees his brother not performing the prayer, or differing from his own prayer in some small details, he goes up to him and says: "What do you know, you have only just started praying, and you know what you used to do, you know what you used to do."

Such people, wallahi (by Allah), risk being distanced from the mercy of Allah. They risk being distanced from the mercy of Allah because of arrogance and because of what they hold in their chests towards their brothers.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَجَعَلْنَا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً أَتَصْبِرُونَ" He says: "And We have made some of you a trial for others." We are a trial for one another, dear brothers, precisely because of these things and because of other things.

He says: "Atasbirun" – He says, "will you be patient?" Will you be patient with one another? Will you set one another right? So if we see that something is wrong with our Muslim brother, approach him kindly, by way of advice – that is what is right.

And not in front of everyone. These, dear brothers, are things, important things. Because the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Rahimallahu abdan…" He says: may Allah have mercy on the servant who says something good, and so, he says, gains some benefit – that is, he gains reward, a good deed. Why?

Because he said something good. Or he stays silent about something ugly that he saw, about something bad that he saw, and so, he says, he is, he is saved. And this should be, this should be constantly on our minds, constantly on our minds, dear brothers: that we respect one another, that we love one another, that we set one another right, that we help one another, because that is what a congregation is.

Only in this way can we, in sha Allah, succeed. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among the true believers. I ask Him, the Exalted, to make us among those who help one another, respect one another, love one another. I ask Him, the Exalted, not to leave even a speck of hatred in our chests towards our Muslim brothers.

I ask Him, the Exalted, to gather us together in Jannah (Paradise). آمين يا رب العالمين. بارك الله لي ولكم في القرآن العظيم، ونفعني وإياكم بما فيه من الآيات والذكر الحكيم. أقول قولي هذا وأستغفر الله لي ولكم فاستغفروه إنه هو الغفور الرحيم.
